title: IT & Admin Credential Governance + Budget Check-in

Some cross-team clarification on rollback plans and timing; agreed to a phased rollout and a small budget request for Q3 tooling subscription.

transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-06-30 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~62 mins | Location: Zoom internal | Recorded by: Fireflies
Attendees (as listed): Sofia M., Jared P., Aditi R., Marcus L., Priya S., Ellen P., Tom R.

00:00 Sofia: okay everyone, let's get started, uh 15:00 on the dot. Thanks for joining the credential governance and budget check-in, I have an agenda — quick status on the rotation plan, cost ask, KMS integration question, and SOC2 artifacts. If we need to reorder say now.
00:18 Jared: sounds good, I'll just flag budget up front, cause that's gating some of the tooling choices.
00:24 Aditi: and I'll tee up risk bits especially around service accounts and ephemeral keys.
00:30 Marcus: also want to make sure platform test coverage is inline with the rotation, so we don't cause a mass outage.
00:36 Sofia: yep, agreed. quick status: runbook draft lives in ops/credentials/rotations but it's skeletal. We intend phased rotation of service-account keys for infra and non-human API keys starting mid-July. We propose weekends for infra-critical but weekday for lower blast radius.
00:52 Priya: mid-July timeline okay but do we have a specific rollback path? last time the repo creds caused cascade failures.
01:00 Marcus: rollback path: we plan to keep old keys valid for 24 hours post-rotation, and smoke tests that hit auth endpoints, DB writes, and worker queues. But we need a fast toggle at the proxy level if things go sideways.
01:15 Aditi: can you confirm which service accounts are in-scope? we need a prioritized list — prod-high, prod-low, staging, etc. We should also categorize by owner and last-used timestamp.
01:29 Marcus: I can generate that from IAM logs, though mapping to owners is a little messy right now.
01:35 Sofia: action: Marcus to produce list by next week.
01:38 Tom: procurement sticker, are we buying KMS HSM-backed keys or using cloud KMS? how much is this gonna cost?
01:45 Jared: initial ask is small — probably 6 HSM seats for Q3 for privileged secret storage, estimate $12k-15k annual run rate. Need to firm up exact SKU though.
02:00 Ellen: for SOC2 we just need evidence that rotations are happening and who approved them; was there an approval workflow previously?
02:07 Aditi: we have ad-hoc approvals via Slack and PRs but no consolidated audit trail. that's why the KMS/SM tool matters. It provides immutable audit logs and key lifecycle events.
02:20 Sofia: so two things: tooling to capture audit log events + runbook with approved owners. 
02:27 Priya: question on SSO/SAML mapping — when we rotate machine-user creds, service principals tied to SSO SAML can break if role mappings change. Are we touching SSO mappings or just keys?
02:38 Aditi: only keys for this wave, but we will do a mapping cleanup next quarter. We'll check role bindings so that token-based auth fallbacks are ok.
02:45 Marcus: quick note — some older jobs still rely on long-lived deploy keys in git, we should identify and rotate or move to short lived tokens.
02:54 Sofia: right, we'll include that in the inventory.
03:00 Jared: on cost, if we centralize secrets in new tool, there are license costs but ops efficiency goes up. we should tie cost to owner buckets so teams pay their share.
03:10 Tom: procurement needs a clear SKU and vendor choice, any preferences? Hashi? cloud vendor native?
03:17 Aditi: leaning Hashi for multi-cloud and robust RBAC, but cloud-native KMS has better native HSM integration. There's tradeoff between audit fidelity and cost.
03:28 Ellen: legal needs SLAs and data residency commitments, esp for EU data — vendor questionnaire will need to be filled.
03:35 Sofia: agreed. Jared, can you draft the procurement ticket with vendor options and cost delta?
03:41 Jared: yes, I'll put it together by July 2.
03:45 03:45 Marcus: on the technical rollback — can we do a canary rotation first? small subset of service accounts and then expand with automated checks.
03:54 Aditi: canary is good. we should codify pass/fail criteria — auth latency within 15% of baseline, zero 5xxs for dependent endpoints, queue lag under X ms.
04:08 Priya: we might need temporary exception policies in the proxy for bursty reauth behavior.
04:14 Sofia: note, include proxy toggles and runbook steps: 1) rotate, 2) run smoke tests, 3) hold old keys for 24h, 4) escalate to oncall if fail.
04:27 Aditi: about secrets manager integration — we need KMS key policies that use HSM protect for the top-level master key, and per-team keys for scoping. That will require IAM changes.
04:40 Marcus: IAM changes means coordination with platform owners and we should deploy IaC changes in canary prior to mass roll.
04:48 Ellen: SOC2 auditors will want to see evidence of who changed policies and when, so all IAM diffs must be in version control and linked to JIRA approvals.
04:58 Sofia: good call. we'll require PR-based policy changes and link to tickets for evidence.
05:05 Jared: about cost ownership — recommend we charge platform and a handful of high-use product teams for the billing line, so ops is not fully on the hook. We'll prepare a cost allocation spreadsheet.
05:18 Marcus: question — will rotation increase API token bill due to re-auth chatter? some clients re-request tokens aggressively.
05:26 Priya: we should measure expected increased token requests; if we need to pay for more request throughput on hosted-API, budget for that.
05:32 Jared: I'll add a 10% contingency to the request.
05:37 Aditi: also want to highlight risk of orphaned service accounts — we need an orphan cleanup job as part of the plan.
05:44 Sofia: agreed, add to runbook. Marcus, can you add orphan detection rules to the list?
05:49 Marcus: will do.
05:52 06:00 ish marker, mid meeting recap: Sofia: recap — runbook, procurement ticket, risk matrix, smoke tests, orphan list. owners assigned. any blockers?
06:06 Ellen: legal will need the vendor questionnaire before procurement closes.
06:10 Tom: procurement needs the SKU by July 2 too.
06:14 Aditi: note, we might need temporary policy exceptions for a week after rotation to allow teams to fix micro-broken integrations. we'll document exception flow.
06:25 Sofia: okay, let's talk timeline. target: start canary July 17, evaluate July 21, expand July 24, complete by end of July for this wave.
06:36 Marcus: that's tight but doable if inventory is ready by July 9.
06:41 Priya: will the oncall rota be changed for the week of July 17? we need extra coverage.
06:46 Sofia: yes, small change; Priya coordinate with SRE.
06:50 06:55 Aditi: technical deep dive follow-up — I'll schedule a 60-min SE-led session next week to go over KMS policy templates and IAM diffs.
06:58 Sofia: great, let's wrap. quick recap of next steps and owners (reads action items). Deadline alignment confirmed.
07:10 Meeting end.

Notes about transcript quality: occasional overlaps and mis-transcribed vendor names (Hashicorp -> Hashi, HSM spelled as H S M sometimes), some speaker labels simplified.
